name: Accelerating Large Language Model Decoding with Speculative Sampling
problem: Same memory-bandwidth bottleneck as Leviathan et al.; addressed with an alternative to sequence-level drafting.
mechanism: Sequence-level speculative sampling: a draft model proposes multiple token sequences (v1 uses independent sequences, v2 conditions the sequence on the previous via Input-level MCMC). Target verifies all candidates in one batched pass; rejection sampling with an independent-sample fallback preserves the exact target distribution within hardware numerics.
speedup_reported: 2x-2.5x decoding speedup for Chinchilla 70B in a DISTRIBUTED setup, versus no speculative sampling, with no sample-quality compromise and no modification to the model. Model pair is 4B draft -> 70B target; the 2-2.5x is a batch-1 latency figure.
notes: VENUE NOTE: no venue is verifiable for this one - Semantic Scholar returns no venue and the arXiv comment field is empty, so venue is recorded as arxiv-preprint with year = arXiv v1 (Feb 2023). It is often cited alongside Leviathan et al. 2211.17192 and the two are independently conceived, contemporaneous, and NOT interchangeable: the arXiv comment on 2211.17192 explicitly cites this paper as concurrent work. Independent-publication nuance matters because acceptance-ratio and drafting-strategy numbers from one paper do not transfer to the other formulation. Code was released later than the paper; the arXiv comment field carries no venue claim.
